author: Justin W
body: Heading into the mid-semester break, we are well into developing the firmware for our sensor node, currently with a working gas, temperature, humidity, and pressure sensor. We have also depeloped a comprehensive CAD model for the entire node and will begin to assemble the physical prototype during break. During the break we also aim to complete all the testing and evaluation.
imageCaption: Kyle and Ken (Firmware team) soldering components

author: Justin W
body: With the Uni semester restarting, we are starting to delve deeper into the prototyping and testing stages of our project. We have split into two teams, one focusing on the firmware, and one focusing on creating and testing the prototype. We expect our knowledge from our research in the first semester will be vital in the process of designing the first prototypes.

title: RFS Communications Team Presentation
author: Justin W
body: We got the opportunity to attend the Rural Fire Service Communications Team presentation, where we gained valuable insights and context into the ways that the RFS communicate with their teams in the field, and how they use data to make decisions. We will take the learnings from our time with the RFS and apply them to our project, ensuring that our work is aligned with the needs of emergency services and the communities they serve.
imageAlt: Four team members standing together at night in front of a NSW Rural Fire Service response van with visible NSW RURAL FIRE SERVICE lettering
imageCaption: The team in front of the RFS Operational Commmand Vehicle

title: Completion of Component Selection Meeting
author: Justin W
body: As we have reached the end of the semester, we have completed the component selection meeting, finalising the key hardware components for the initial sensor node prototype. The next steps involve procuring the components and beginning the design and assembly of the first prototype for field testing in Semester 2.

title: Mid-Project Presentation and Workstream Reports Update
author: Justin W
body: With the mid-project presentation and workstream reports complete, we are now focused on preparing for the next milestone, creating the first prototypes of the sensor node and beginning testing.

title: Workstream Progress Update
author: Justin W
body: Research is well underway across all three workstreams. The Power and Enclosure Report has been completed with recommendations for solar panel sizing and battery capacity. The network and sensors workstreams are progressing well and are on track to be completed by the end of phase 1.
